data.text:
Approve gated command 'pins.regenerate' for agent padap2?  [request Qd6903a86fb]
  command : ddflow pins regenerate [--only NAME] --approval request|ID
  item    : -    target: -
  acts on : the pin files as recorded before the re-record
  digest  : 5d09a9f0f836830b  (the state is read again when the agent runs it)
  needs   : tier T2, assurance level L1 or stronger; 1 use(s)
  args    : only=
  agent's reason (untrusted, not part of the approval): ""

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier untriaged “cancel cannot interrupt an active prompt” defect still holds in the new code: `serve` processes one JSON-RPC frame at a time, and `_prompt` calls `on_prompt` before the loop can read the next line. Given `AcpStdioAgent(write, on_prompt=slow_on_prompt)` where `slow_on_prompt` sleeps for one second, and an input stream containing a `session/prompt` request followed immediately by a `session/cancel` notification, the cancel frame is not fetched or handled until `slow_on_prompt` has already returned. `session.cancelled` therefore stays `False` during the turn, `_prompt` resets it to `False` anyway, and the client receives `stopReason: "end_turn"` (or the callback’s reason) instead of `"cancelled"`. Cancellation over the same stdio wire cannot work through the default `serve` path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioAgent.serve / AcpStdioAgent._prompt

chunk_findings.detail: Non-OK outcomes are dereferenced as if they always contain a dictionary `result`. `_ask` returns `Outcome(UNAVAILABLE, detail=...)` when there is no channel, and `_exchange` returns `done(ERROR/EOF/TIMEOUT, ...)` without setting `result`; those non-OK outcomes have `result=None`. Therefore `new_session` crashes at `sid = out.result.get("sessionId")` and `prompt` crashes at `merged.stop_reason = str(out.result.get("stopReason", ""))`. For example, calling `AcpStdioClient(starter, ["agent"]).new_session("/tmp", [], 1.0)` before `connect` should return an unavailable session object, but it raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'`. The same happens when the agent replies to `session/new` or `session/prompt` with a JSON-RPC error response.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioClient.new_session / AcpStdioClient.prompt

chunk_findings.detail: `_on_other` assumes every frame’s `params` is dictionary-like. The expression `(msg.get("params") or {})` yields the original non-empty list if `params` is a JSON-RPC array, and the next line calls `.get` on it. Given a valid JSON-RPC frame such as `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"session/update","params":[]}` (or `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"session/request_permission","params":[]}`), the adapter raises `AttributeError` inside `seen`, aborting `prompt()` and returning no `PromptResult`. For a permission request with no policy, the documented behavior is to refuse it, not to crash.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioClient._on_other

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeAcpClient.prompt` dereferences `out.result` before checking `out.status`. `_ask` returns `A.Outcome(A.ERROR, error=reply["error"])` with no result when the fake agent replies with a JSON-RPC error. Given a connected client and an unknown session id, `prompt("missing", "hi", 1.0)` makes the agent return an `INVALID_PARAMS` error for the unknown session, `_ask` returns an error outcome whose `result` is `None`, and line 168 raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'` instead of returning a `PromptResult` carrying the error status. The same unchecked dereference exists at line 151 in `new_session`, where any error reply from the agent makes `out.result.get("sessionId")` crash.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py:168

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeAcpAgent._prompt` uses one mutable `session.cancelled` flag with no association to the prompt turn. Given a connected client and session, `prompt(...)` returns `end_turn`; then `cancel(session_id)` sets `session.cancelled = True`; the next `prompt(...)` reads that stale flag at line 90 and returns `A.CANCELLED`, even though the cancel arrived after the previous turn had already completed. The comment says a cancel ends one turn, but this fake arms the following prompt instead.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py:90

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeAcpAgent.handle` treats `session/cancel` as a notification before checking whether the incoming message is a JSON-RPC request. Given `{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "session/cancel", "params": {"sessionId": "s1"}}`, it marks the session cancelled if known and returns `None`, giving no response to a message that has an `id`. A request-shaped `session/cancel` should receive an error/refusal response; otherwise a conformance case or `_ask`-style caller can wait or assert instead of getting a reply.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py:47

chunk_findings.detail: The fake passes `A.UNAVAILABLE` to callers, contradicting the stated conformance rule that unavailable is never passed [D-adapters-answers]. `FakeAcpClient(mode="unavailable").connect(1.0)` returns an `A.AcpHandshake` whose status is `A.UNAVAILABLE` at line 133, and `new_session` line 149 plus `prompt` line 163 also return `A.UNAVAILABLE` when `connect` was not called first. This lets a consumer using the fake observe the exact status the port is supposed not to pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py:133

chunk_findings.detail: The documented cancel contract is wrong for ACP: `session/cancel` is meant to cancel the prompt turn that is currently running, but this line defines it as arming the *next* turn that finishes. Given an agent that completes a prompt with `end_turn`, a client that then sends `session/cancel` (for example, a user pressing stop after the response has already returned, or a race where the cancel arrives just after the prompt response) will cause the following unrelated prompt to return `cancelled`. Conversely, while a prompt is running, the same “reads one frame at a time” model means the cancel cannot be observed until that prompt has already finished, so the current turn is not cancelled. This documents a non-conforming and misleading port for DSH-lane-acp and VB-acp adopters.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/adapters/acp.md:14

chunk_findings.detail: The conformance requirement says “unavailable is never passed”, but this test makes `A.UNAVAILABLE` a required observable: for either maker, a client that has not been connected must return `A.UNAVAILABLE` from `new_session("/w", [], 1)` and `prompt("s1", "x", 1)`. Given `make("default")()` or `make("fake")()` without calling `connect`, the test only passes if the adapter/fake surfaces the forbidden status, so the test codifies a contract violation [D-adapters-answers].
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_acp.py:test_a_client_that_is_not_connected_is_unavailable

chunk_findings.detail: The test constructs `FakeAcpAgent()` with no arguments, while every other fake-agent construction in the file supplies a `Script` (`_fake`, `_agents`, and `CONFORMANCE["AcpAgent"]["fake"]` all use `SCRIPT`). If `FakeAcpAgent.__init__` requires the scripted session, this line raises `TypeError: __init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'script'` before any `isinstance` assertion runs, so the port-registration test fails.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_acp.py:test_the_adapter_and_the_fake_satisfy_the_ports

chunk_findings.detail: `new_session` does `sid = out.result.get("sessionId")` and `prompt` does `out.result.get("stopReason", "")` without first checking `out.status`. `_ask` and `_exchange` return `Outcome` objects with `result=None` for `UNAVAILABLE`, `ERROR`, `TIMEOUT`, and `EOF` outcomes. Given `client = AcpStdioClient(starter, ["agent"]); client.new_session("/tmp", [], 1.0)` before `connect`, `_ask` returns `Outcome(UNAVAILABLE, detail="not connected: call connect first")` with `result=None`, so the next line raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'`. The same crash occurs after an agent JSON-RPC error in `prompt`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py AcpStdioClient.new_session, AcpStdioClient.prompt

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding #7 still holds: the server read loop is synchronous. `serve` delegates to `StdioServer.serve(lines, self.handle)`, and `handle` blocks inside `_prompt` while `on_prompt` runs. A `session/cancel` notification arriving during the prompt is not read until `on_prompt` returns, so `session.cancelled` is never set while the turn is active. With a client that sends `session/prompt` and then `session/cancel` while a long-running `on_prompt` is working, the prompt finishes normally and returns its normal `stopReason` instead of `"cancelled"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py AcpStdioAgent.serve / AcpStdioAgent._prompt

chunk_findings.detail: When an agent sends a `session/request_permission` frame whose `params` is a JSON array rather than an object (valid JSON-RPC params shape), `_on_other` assigns `params = msg.get("params") or {}` and then calls `params.get("toolCall")`. A list has no `.get`, so the client raises `AttributeError` instead of refusing the malformed permission request. Example agent frame while a prompt is waiting: `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"session/request_permission","params":[]}` with `permission=None`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py AcpStdioClient._on_other

chunk_findings.detail: `_ask` can return an `A.Outcome` with status `A.ERROR` and `result=None` when the fake agent returns a JSON-RPC error, but these methods dereference `out.result` without checking `out.status`. A connected client calling `prompt("missing", "hi", 1.0)` makes `FakeAcpAgent.handle` return the unknown-session error, then `prompt` executes `out.result.get("stopReason", "")` and raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'` instead of returning a `PromptResult` carrying the error status. The same fault is in `connect` (`out.result.get("agentInfo")`) and `new_session` (`out.result.get("sessionId")`).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py FakeAcpClient.connect / new_session / prompt

chunk_findings.detail: The change’s stated conformance requirement says “unavailable is never passed,” but this fake explicitly passes `A.UNAVAILABLE` to callers. `FakeAcpClient(mode="unavailable").connect(1.0)` returns an `A.AcpHandshake` with status `A.UNAVAILABLE`, and `new_session`/`prompt` return `A.UNAVAILABLE` when `connect` was not called first. A consumer using the fake therefore observes the exact status the port must never pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py FakeAcpClient.connect / new_session / prompt

chunk_findings.detail: The permission-ask handling assumes `ask.get("toolCall")` is dict-like whenever truthy. With `Script(asks=[{"toolCall": "bad"}])` and `permission=lambda _: None`, line 176 evaluates `("bad" or {}).get("title", "")` and raises `AttributeError`; with no policy the intended behavior is to refuse the permission request, not crash.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py FakeAcpClient.prompt

chunk_findings.detail: The `session/cancel` branch returns `None` before checking whether the incoming message has an `id`, so a JSON-RPC request-shaped cancel receives no response. Given `FakeAcpAgent().handle({"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":9,"method":"session/cancel","params":{"sessionId":"s1"}})`, `handle` returns `None`; a caller waiting for that request response can hang. A message with an `id` must be answered, even if the method is usually a notification.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py FakeAcpAgent.handle

chunk_findings.detail: The new documentation states that `AcpStdioAgent.serve` reads one frame at a time and therefore sees `session/cancel` only between turns, so a cancel frame sent while `on_prompt` is running cannot interrupt that prompt; it remains unread until the prompt has already finished. This is the same defect as previous finding 7, and the documentation confirms the default adapter does not actually support canceling a running ACP session/prompt over stdio. The suggested workaround—feeding frames from a second thread and watching `session.cancelled` inside `on_prompt`—is not available to an ordinary ACP-over-stdio client, so the advertised `session/cancel` support is false. Example: a client sends `session/prompt` and then `session/cancel` during a slow prompt; the prompt returns normally instead of `cancelled`.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/adapters/acp.md:14

chunk_findings.detail: The change’s conformance requirement says “unavailable is never passed,” but this test asserts that both the real and fake `AcpClient` return `A.UNAVAILABLE` when not connected (`client.new_session("/w", [], 1).status == A.UNAVAILABLE` and `client.prompt("s1", "x", 1).status == A.UNAVAILABLE`), and the `mode="unavailable"` parameterization likewise asserts `hello.status == A.UNAVAILABLE`. The contract test therefore formalizes exactly the status the port must never pass, so the forbidden status is observable by consumers of the fake and the real adapter.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_acp.py:test_a_client_that_is_not_connected_is_unavailable

chunk_findings.detail: The documented “by design” note does not fix cancel. `serve` still reads one frame at a time and `_prompt` still calls `on_prompt` to completion before `handle` can see another line; the new `active` flag is only set inside that blocked call. Given `AcpStdioAgent(write, on_prompt=slow)` where `slow` sleeps one second and polls `session.cancelled`, and stdin containing `session/prompt` immediately followed by `session/cancel`, the cancel stays unread until `slow` returns, so `session.cancelled` is never true during the turn and the prompt response is `end_turn` rather than `cancelled`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioAgent.serve / AcpStdioAgent._prompt

chunk_findings.detail: `close` is specified safe to call while a turn is in flight, but the read loop uses `self._channel` after `close` has already nulled it. Given a connected client whose `prompt` is blocked in `receive`, a second thread calling `close()` sets `self._channel` to `None`; the next line `self._channel.receive(...)` raises `AttributeError` instead of returning an `EOF`/`UNAVAILABLE` `PromptResult`. `_send` already treats a missing channel as a failed send, so this path is inconsistent with that.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioClient._exchange

chunk_findings.detail: `prompt` always walks `self.agent.script.asks` after `_ask`, including when the turn never started. Given a connected `FakeAcpClient` whose agent `Script` has `asks=[{}]` (or any ask the policy refuses / `permission=None`), `prompt("missing", "hi", 1.0)` makes `FakeAcpAgent._prompt` return `INVALID_PARAMS` for the unknown session, then the ask loop still runs, appends a permission, and sets `stop_reason` to `A.CANCELLED`. The caller gets an error outcome whose stop reason says the turn was cancelled, which is wrong because no session was prompted and no ask was actually in that turn.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py:FakeAcpClient.prompt

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten cancel note still does not make a running turn cancellable, and the workaround it now prescribes cannot do so either. It states that `AcpStdioAgent.serve` reads one frame at a time and therefore only observes `session/cancel` between turns (so an in-flight cancel is ignored), then tells a caller that must interrupt a running turn to feed frames from a second thread and watch `session.cancelled` inside `on_prompt`. Feeding another frame onto the same stdio iterator does not run `handle` while `serve` is blocked inside `on_prompt`, so `session.cancelled` stays unset for that turn and the prompt still finishes as a normal completion. Given `session/prompt` then `session/cancel` while `on_prompt` is still running, the cancel remains unread until the turn has already ended; the idle-cancel no-op then drops it. [previous findings 1, 12, 18 still hold; the new workaround does not answer them]
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/adapters/acp.md:14

data.probe: acp.py AcpStdioAgent.serve->StdioServer.serve loops lines calling handle; _prompt (line 264) calls self._on_prompt(...) synchronously and only returns after the turn ends, so session/cancel on the same iterator is read after _prompt already set session.active=False (line 266); handle then sets session.cancelled=session.active (line 215)=False. Verified in source: no concurrent read, cancel during flight is a no-op.
data.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioAgent.serve / AcpStdioAgent._prompt

data.probe: mcp.py _ChannelClient.close() sets self._channel=None; acp.py _exchange line 436 dereferences self._channel.receive(...) with a type-ignore, no local capture, so a concurrent close() during the receive raises AttributeError instead of an EOF/UNAVAILABLE Outcome (while _send already returns False on a missing channel via send_line). Verified in source.
data.title: ddflow/adapters/acp.py:AcpStdioClient._exchange

data.probe: fakes/acp.py FakeAcpClient.prompt lines 177-184 run the script.asks loop unconditionally after _ask; for an unknown session FakeAcpAgent._prompt returns INVALID_PARAMS ERROR, yet the loop appends a permission and sets stop_reason=CANCELLED on an ERROR outcome. Verified in source.
data.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/acp.py:FakeAcpClient.prompt

data.probe: acp.py serve is blocked inside _prompt (on_prompt), not in reading lines, so the docs workaround (feed session/cancel from a second thread) cannot run handle mid-turn; the cancel is read only after the turn ends. Verified in source; same root cause as #20.
data.title: docs/ddflow/adapters/acp.md:14

evidence.note: CONFIRMED: the gh/glab CLI contracts the forge family moves behind the port are unchanged. The port re-homes the SAME _run/_check/_json shell-out (gh pr list|view|create|merge|edit --json fields from the gh manual; GitLab REST via glab api) with no behaviour change — READ NOW in ddflow/adapters/forge.py + forge_gitlab.py. Probe: tests/test_adapter_forge.py CONFORMANCE runs find/view/merge/set_base/threads/reply/resolve against BOTH a scripted runner and FakeForge (venue the conformance harness runs against adapter AND fake).

Applied r-adapters (one port, one implementation per function), D-adapters-answers/D-adapters-answers-2 (port=Protocol next to default adapter + registry, fake in fakes/, conformance test), r-small-files (GitLab split to forge_gitlab.py to stay <20KB), r-reuse-core (Registry[T] keyed by name), D-unify strangler (behaviour-preserving move). baselines only shrink: deleted tests/guard_baselines/ports_without_fake/Forge.txt now that FakeForge ships.

Moved forge family to ddflow.adapters.forge (Forge Protocol + PRInfo/Thread + GitHub(gh) + GitLab(glab) + FORGES registry) with infra.forge as a compat shim keeping detect(); moved the pure text clipper to ddflow.adapters.textcut (core.textcut re-exports); archifaces re-homes gh/glab to the adapter modules; added FakeForge + tests/test_adapter_forge.py conformance.

chunk_findings.detail: `_answer` appends to `calls` and only then raises `script[method]`, but the module contract says a canned `ForgeUnavailable`/`ForgeError` is raised before the call records. Script `script["view"] = ForgeError(...)` and call `view(1)`: the exception is raised and `calls == [("view", 1)]`, so a test that treats a scripted failure as “never asked” (as documented) sees a recorded call that did not happen on the real adapter.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/forge.py:30

chunk_findings.detail: The fake’s stated job is to record every argument a caller asked for, but `create` records only `(head, base, title)`, `merge` only `(number, strategy)`, and `reply` only `(number, thread_id)`. `create(head="h", base="main", title="t", body="body", draft=True, labels=["L"], reviewers=["r"])` leaves `("create", "h", "main", "t")` and drops body, draft, labels, and reviewers; `merge(1, strategy="squash", head_sha="abc", auto=True)` drops `head_sha` and `auto`; `reply(1, "th", "please fix")` drops the body. Those calls cannot be asserted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/forge.py:42

chunk_findings.detail: `set_base` updates `requests` only when the number is already present, while `view` fabricates a `PRInfo` for a missing number. With an empty table, `set_base(1, "dev")` then `view(1)` returns `PRInfo(number=1)` whose base is not `"dev"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/forge.py:58

chunk_findings.detail: `strategy="ff-only"` is mapped to `gh pr merge --rebase`, and any other value except `"squash"` becomes `--merge`. Fast-forward-only must refuse a non-ancestor head; `--rebase` replays commits and can still merge that PR. Separately, `strategy="rebase"` is not in the dict, so it falls through to `--merge` and creates a merge commit instead of a rebase.
chunk_findings.title: GitHub.merge

chunk_findings.detail: A completed check whose `conclusion` is `STALE` is in neither `_GH_FAILED` nor `_GH_OK`, and `status == "COMPLETED"` skips the pending branch, so the rollup is reported `"passing"`. Input `[{"status": "COMPLETED", "conclusion": "STALE"}]` returns `"passing"`, which treats an obsolete check as green.
chunk_findings.title: _gh_checks

chunk_findings.detail: `find` calls `projects/:id/merge_requests` with `source_branch` and `state=all` but no `per_page` and no page walk. GitLab defaults to 20 rows, ordered `created_at` desc. Given 21 historical merge requests on branch `foo` whose only `opened` one is the oldest, the open request is not on page 1; the sort then picks the newest closed row and `view` returns that MR instead of the open one.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/forge_gitlab.py:find

chunk_findings.detail: `whole_marks` only drops from the last `[REDACTED:` and treats any later `]` as a closer, so a head that contains two unclosed starts still ends inside the first mark. `clip("pre [REDACTED: aa [REDACTED: bb" + "x"*40, limit=5, keep=30, marker="…")` keeps a prefix like `"pre [REDACTED: aa …"`, which is the leak this helper exists to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/textcut.py:36

chunk_findings.detail: `_after_mark` only matches a finished `\[REDACTED:[^\]]*\]`, so `window` (and tail `clip`) will start inside an unclosed mark and emit its body. For `text="abcdefghij[REDACTED:password123"`, `window(text, 20, 8)` returns `"…password"` (start 20 is past `[REDACTED:` and there is no `]`), contradicting the guarantee that a window neither starts nor ends inside a redaction mark.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/textcut.py:45

chunk_findings.detail: The replacement file is 33 lines (`@@ -1,681 +1,33 @@`) and ends on `def detect(repo: Path, cfg: Config) -> Forge:` with no suite. Importing `ddflow.infra.forge` raises `SyntaxError` (expected indented block) before any caller can run. The module docstring says `detect` stays here because it reads configuration and the worktree remote, and `shutil`, `UnknownName`, `Config`, and `git` are imported for that body, but the body was deleted with the rest of the old module. Any `detect(repo, cfg)` call, including a GitHub remote with a configured forge name, never returns a `Forge`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/forge.py:33

chunk_findings.detail: `find` calls `projects/:id/merge_requests` with `source_branch` and `state=all` but no `per_page` and no page walk. GitLab defaults to 20 rows, ordered `created_at` desc. Given 21 historical merge requests on branch `foo` whose only `opened` one is the oldest, the open request is not on page 1; the sort then picks the newest closed row and `view` returns that MR instead of the open one.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/forge_gitlab.py:find

chunk_findings.detail: `whole_marks` only drops from the last `[REDACTED:` and treats any later `]` as a closer, so a head that contains two unclosed starts still ends inside the first mark. `clip("pre [REDACTED: aa [REDACTED: bb" + "x"*40, limit=5, keep=30, marker="…")` keeps a prefix like `"pre [REDACTED: aa …"`, which is the leak this helper exists to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/textcut.py:36

chunk_findings.detail: `_after_mark` only matches a finished `\[REDACTED:[^\]]*\]`, so `window` (and tail `clip`) will start inside an unclosed mark and emit its body. For `text="abcdefghij[REDACTED:password123"`, `window(text, 20, 8)` returns `"…password"` (start 20 is past `[REDACTED:` and there is no `]`), contradicting the guarantee that a window neither starts nor ends inside a redaction mark.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/textcut.py:45

chunk_findings.detail: The replacement file is 33 lines (`@@ -1,681 +1,33 @@`) and ends on `def detect(repo: Path, cfg: Config) -> Forge:` with no suite. Importing `ddflow.infra.forge` raises `SyntaxError` (expected indented block) before any caller can run. The module docstring says `detect` stays here because it reads configuration and the worktree remote, and `shutil`, `UnknownName`, `Config`, and `git` are imported for that body, but the body was deleted with the rest of the old module. Any `detect(repo, cfg)` call, including a GitHub remote with a configured forge name, never returns a `Forge`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/forge.py:33

chunk_findings.detail: `_run` is the shared CLI ask path, but after a non-timeout failure it returns `done.unwrap()` and never maps stderr through `_UNAVAILABLE_HINTS` the way `_check` does. Given `gh` installed and not logged in, `P.capture(["gh", ...])` returns non-zero with stderr containing `auth login` / `not logged`; `timed_out` is false, so the caller gets whatever `unwrap()` raises (not `ForgeUnavailable`). The module contract treats "could not be asked" (not logged in, host unresolved, connection refused) as `ForgeUnavailable`, distinct from a forge refusal; this path collapses that case into a generic process error.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/forge.py:_run

chunk_findings.detail: `reply` sends the comment through `gh api graphql -f body=...`. gh treats a `-f`/`-F` value that starts with `@` as a local file path. Given body `@README` (or any `@/path/to/file`), the mutation does not post that text: gh reads the file and either fails the call or publishes the file contents as the review reply.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/forge.py:GitHub.reply

chunk_findings.detail: `strategy="ff-only"` is mapped to `gh pr merge --rebase`. `--rebase` replays commits onto the base and succeeds when the head is not a fast-forward; it also rewrites SHAs. A caller that asked for a fast-forward-only merge therefore gets a rebase merge (or a success where ff-only should have refused). Unknown strategy strings fall through to `--merge` the same way.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/forge.py:GitHub.merge

chunk_findings.detail: `threads` requests `per_page=100` and never follows later pages. GitLab caps a page at 100 and defaults to oldest-first, so an MR with 101 resolvable discussions drops the newest one. Given !5 with 100 already-resolved threads and a 101st unresolved review on page 2, `threads(5)` returns only the resolved set; a caller that merges when every returned thread is resolved will merge with an open review still on the MR.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/forge_gitlab.py:threads

chunk_findings.detail: `strategy` is only consulted for `squash`. Any other value, including `"rebase"`, is sent as `squash=false` and GitLab then merges with the project default (usually a merge commit). `merge(1, strategy="rebase", head_sha="abc", auto=False)` therefore succeeds with a merge commit and never calls the rebase API, so the caller’s requested history rewrite does not happen and is not reported as an error.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/forge_gitlab.py:merge

chunk_findings.detail: After `glab mr create` exits 0, a miss from `find` raises `ForgeUnavailable` rather than `ForgeError`. That type means the forge was declined or offline. Given a successful create whose `source_branch` filter does not match (branch passed as `refs/heads/feature`, or the new MR not yet visible), the adapter reports the forge as unavailable even though the MR was created. A caller that treats unavailable as “retry the whole operation” will try to create again against a branch that already has a request.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/forge_gitlab.py:create

chunk_findings.detail: `boundary="word"` runs after `whole_marks` and is never rechecked, so a head can end inside a redaction mark. For `clip("prefix [REDACTED:hello world]END", limit=29, boundary="word")` the 29-character head is `prefix [REDACTED:hello world]` (the `]` is still present, so `whole_marks` keeps it) and `rsplit(" ", 1)[0]` cuts on the space inside the mark, returning `prefix [REDACTED:hello`. That breaks the stated invariant that a head never ends inside `[REDACTED:...]`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/textcut.py:94

Importing `ddflow.infra.forge` raises SyntaxError before any forge call; a completed body would still be required for the documented entry point.
